html:
British rule over Cyprus began in 1878, when the Ottoman Empire let Britain run the island in return for help against Russia, and lasted until independence in 1960.

Britain wanted a base to guard the route to the Suez Canal. It annexed Cyprus in 1914 when the Ottomans joined World War I, and made it a crown colony in 1925. Greek Cypriots, about four fifths of the people, increasingly demanded enosis, union with Greece, and burned Government House in 1931. Turkish Cypriots opposed this. Britain, needing the island after losing Suez, used Turkish Cypriot police against the EOKA revolt. Independence left Britain two sovereign military bases, which it still holds.
sum: British rule over Cyprus began in 1878, when the Ottoman Empire let Britain run the island in return for help against Russia, and lasted until independence in 1960.
